    LargeIndecomposable.ZeroColumn.zeroColumn

    Block matrices with a zero column #

    Lemma 4.3 of the manuscript. Let Ω be a finite set with a partition, given by a map p : Ω → P whose fibres are the parts, and let M i be vector spaces. Endomorphisms of ⨁ M i = Π i, M i are block matrices with blocks block f j i : M i → M j (columns are indexed by sources). The diagonal part diag f keeps the blocks block f i i.

    For a unital subalgebra E preserving the part-subspaces, with

    1. diag E ⊆ E,
    2. every coordinate map E₀ = diag E → End(M i) injective,
    3. N = ker (diag|_E) spanned by elements of N with at most one nonzero block in each row and column and with a zero column,

    diag : E → E₀ is a split algebra surjection, N is a two-sided ideal, and every product of m elements of N vanishes, m the largest part size.

    The proof needs neither M i ≠ 0 nor Ω ≠ ∅, nor the row condition in (3); the core lemmas are stated without them, and zeroColumn states the lemma with the manuscript's hypotheses.
